description: Inbound social sign-in (Google, GitHub, Microsoft) with account linking and CSRF-protected callbacks, ported from the existing implementation.

requirements.description: Users must be able to sign in via OAuth2/OIDC social providers (Google, GitHub, Microsoft). The OAuth callback flow must be protected against CSRF via state parameter stored in Redis with expiry. After successful provider authentication, the service links the external identity to a local account (by verified email or explicit link action). Linked accounts appear in the user's self-service UI. Each provider is configured per realm.
requirements.deferred_reason: Inbound social federation is outside this plan; the authenticator remains a local account authority with typed relying-party integration.
requirements.revisit_trigger: An operator needs Google, GitHub, Microsoft, or another external identity provider for sign-in.
requirements.title: OAuth2/OIDC Social Federation with Account Linking and CSRF Protection

validation.notes: api/internal/oauth/csrf_test.go: state nonce is generated, stored in Redis with TTL; callback with matching state succeeds and consumes the nonce; replay of the same state is rejected
api/internal/oauth/provider_test.go: mock provider returns user info; account linking logic matches by verified email and creates a linked identity record

api/handlers/oauth/callback_e2e_test.go: initiate OAuth flow for a stubbed Google provider, receive redirect with state; submit callback with correct state and mock token → local session issued; replay callback with same state → rejected
api/handlers/oauth/callback_e2e_test.go: user with existing email account signs in via social provider with matching verified email → accounts linked; subsequent sign-in via either method works
bas/auth/social_signin_test: user clicks 'Sign in with Google' (mocked provider), completes OAuth flow, and arrives at authenticated state with linked account visible in profile
